items.stem:
250 apples of a box were weighted and the distribution of masses of the apples is given in the following table :
Mass (in grams)80-100100-120120-140140-160160-180
Number of apples206070x60
(i) Find the value of x and the mean mass of the apples. (ii) Find the modal mass of the apples.
items.answer:
(i) The frequencies must add to 250, so 20 + 60 + 70 + x + 60 = 250, i.e. 210 + x = 250 and x = 40. Taking class marks 90, 110, 130, 150, 170 the products fᵢxᵢ are 1800, 6600, 9100, 6000 and 10200, so Σfᵢxᵢ = 33700 with Σfᵢ = 250. Mean = 33700 ÷ 250 = 134.8 g.
(ii) The largest frequency is 70, so the modal class is 120−140, with l = 120, f₁ = 70, f₀ = 60, f₂ = 40 and h = 20. Mode = 120 + [(70 − 60)/(2×70 − 60 − 40)] × 20 = 120 + (10/40) × 20 = 120 + 5 = 125.
Hence x = 40, the mean mass is 134.8 g and the modal mass is 125 g.
items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2023 OD Standard
items.ocr: The printed mode line lists 'f₂ = 60' but the book's own substitution uses 40 (the 140−160 frequency), which is right; the last step is also printed as 120 + (20/40)×10, a typo for (10/40)×20. Both reach the printed answer 125.

Compute the mode for the following frequency distribution:
Size of items (in cm)0-44-88-1212-1616-2020-2424-28
Frequency5791712106
items.answer: The greatest frequency is 17, so the modal class is 12−16. Here l = 12, f₁ = 17, f₀ = 9, f₂ = 12 and h = 4. Mode = l + [(f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h = 12 + [(17 − 9)/(2×17 − 9 − 12)] × 4 = 12 + (8/13) × 4 = 12 + 2.46. Hence the mode is 14.46 cm.

items.stem:
The mean of the following frequency distribution is 18. The frequency f in the class interval 19-21 is missing. Determine f.
Class interval11-1313-1515-1717-1919-2121-2323-25
Frequency36913f54
items.answer: The class marks are 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22 and 24, giving fᵢxᵢ of 36, 84, 144, 234, 20f, 110 and 96. So Σfᵢ = 40 + f and Σfᵢxᵢ = 704 + 20f. Using mean = Σfᵢxᵢ/Σfᵢ, 18 = (704 + 20f)/(40 + f), so 720 + 18f = 704 + 20f, giving 2f = 16. Hence f = 8.

Class15-2020-2525-3030-3535-4040-45

items.answer: The maximum frequency is 10, so the modal class is 30−35. Here l = 30, f₀ = 9, f₁ = 10, f₂ = 3 and h = 5. Mode = 30 + [(10 − 9)/(2×10 − 9 − 3)] × 5 = 30 + (1/8) × 5 = 30 + 0.625. Hence the mode is 30.625.

items.stem:
The marks obtained by 110 students in an examination are given below
Marks30-3535-4040-4545-5050-5555-6060-65
Number of Students141628231883
Find the mean marks of the students.
items.answer: Take the assumed mean a = 47.5 (the class mark of 45−50) and h = 5, so uᵢ = (xᵢ − 47.5)/5 runs −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. The products fᵢuᵢ are −42, −32, −28, 0, 18, 16 and 9, so Σfᵢuᵢ = −59 with N = 110. Mean = a + (Σfᵢuᵢ/N) × h = 47.5 + (−59/110) × 5 = 47.5 − 2.682. Hence the mean marks are 44.818, about 44.82.

items.stem:
The mean of the following distribution is 48 and sum of all the frequency is 50. Find the missing frequencies x and y.
Class20-3030-4040-5050-6060-70
Frequency86x11y
items.answer: Take a = 45 and h = 10, so uᵢ = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and fᵢuᵢ = −16, −6, 0, 11, 2y, giving Σfᵢuᵢ = 2y − 11. The total frequency is Σfᵢ = 25 + x + y = 50. From mean = a + (Σfᵢuᵢ/Σfᵢ) × h, 48 = 45 + [(2y − 11)/50] × 10, so 3 = (2y − 11)/5, i.e. 15 = 2y − 11 and y = 13. Then x + y = 25 gives x = 25 − 13 = 12. Hence x = 12 and y = 13.

items.stem:
The table below shows the daily expenditure on food of 25 households in a locality. Find the mean daily expenditure on food.
Daily expenditure (in ₹)100-150150-200200-250250-300300-350
Number of households451222
items.answer: Take the assumed mean a = 225 and h = 50. The class marks are 125, 175, 225, 275, 325, so uᵢ = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and fᵢuᵢ = −8, −5, 0, 2, 4, giving Σfᵢuᵢ = −7 with Σfᵢ = 25. Mean = a + (Σfᵢuᵢ/Σfᵢ) × h = 225 + (−7/25) × 50 = 225 − 14 = 211. Hence the mean daily expenditure on food is ₹211.

items.stem:
The weekly expenditure of 500 families is tabulated below :
Weekly Expenditure (Rs.)Number of families
0-1000150
1000-2000200
2000-300075
3000-400060
4000-500015
Find the median expenditure.
items.answer: The cumulative frequencies are 150, 350, 425, 485 and 500, so N = 500 and N/2 = 250. The first cumulative frequency greater than 250 is 350, so the median class is 1000−2000, with l = 1000, F = 150, f = 200 and h = 1000. Median = l + [(N/2 − F)/f] × h = 1000 + [(250 − 150)/200] × 1000 = 1000 + 500 = 1500. Hence the median weekly expenditure is Rs. 1500.

items.stem:
Following frequency distribution shows the expenditure on milk of 30 households in a locality :
Daily expenditure on milk (Rs.)0-3030-6060-9090-120120-150
Number of households56964
Find the mode for the above data.
items.answer: The greatest frequency is 9, so the modal class is 60−90, with l = 60, f₁ = 9, f₀ = 6, f₂ = 6 and h = 30. Mode = 60 + [(9 − 6)/(2×9 − 6 − 6)] × 30 = 60 + (3/6) × 30 = 60 + 15 = 75. Hence the modal daily expenditure on milk is Rs. 75.

items.stem:
Find the median of the following data :
Height (in cm)Less than 120Less than 140Less than 160Less than 180Less than 200
Number of students1226344050
items.answer: Turning the 'less than' figures into class frequencies gives 100−120 : 12, 120−140 : 14, 140−160 : 8, 160−180 : 6 and 180−200 : 10, with cumulative frequencies 12, 26, 34, 40, 50. So N = 50 and N/2 = 25. The first cumulative frequency greater than 25 is 26, so the median class is 120−140, with l = 120, F = 12, f = 14 and h = 20. Median = 120 + [(25 − 12)/14] × 20 = 120 + 260/14 = 120 + 18.57. Hence the median height is 138.57 cm.

items.stem:
The mean of the following distribution is 31.4. Determine the missing frequency x.
Class0-1010-2020-3030-4040-5050-60
Frequency5x101278
items.answer: Take a = 35 (the class mark of 30−40) and h = 10, so uᵢ = −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and fᵢuᵢ = −15, −2x, −10, 0, 7, 16, giving Σfᵢuᵢ = −2x − 2 and Σfᵢ = 42 + x. From mean = a + (Σfᵢuᵢ/Σfᵢ) × h, 31.4 = 35 + [(−2x − 2)/(42 + x)] × 10, so (2x + 2) × 10 = (42 + x) × 3.6, i.e. 20x + 20 = 151.2 + 3.6x, giving 16.4x = 131.2. Hence x = 8.
items.ocr: The stem is printed as 'the mean ... is 314', but the worked solution uses 31.4 at every step and only 31.4 is consistent with classes 0-60, so the solution wins and the stem is corrected to 31.4. The solution table also misprints the first class as 1-10 (it is 0-10) and the frequency total as 42+2 (it is 42+x).

items.stem:
Calculate the mean of the following frequency distribution :
Class10-3030-5050-7070-9090-110
Frequency151825102
items.answer: The class marks are 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100. Take the assumed mean a = 60 and h = 20, so uᵢ = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and fᵢuᵢ = −30, −18, 0, 10, 4, giving Σfᵢuᵢ = −34 with Σfᵢ = 70. Mean = a + (Σfᵢuᵢ/Σfᵢ) × h = 60 + (−34/70) × 20 = 60 − 9.71. Hence the mean is 50.29.
items.ocr: No board tag is printed against this solution. The book writes 'mid point of class 50-60' where it means the class 50-70, whose mid point is the 60 it actually uses.

items.stem:
Heights of students of class X are given in the following distribution :
Heights (in cm)150-155155-160160-165165-170170-175
Number of students15820125
Find the modal height.
items.answer: The greatest frequency is 20, so the modal class is 160−165, with l = 160, f₁ = 20, f₀ = 8, f₂ = 12 and h = 5. Mode = 160 + [(20 − 8)/(2×20 − 8 − 12)] × 5 = 160 + (12/20) × 5 = 160 + 3 = 163. Hence the modal height is 163 cm.

items.stem:
A school conducted a test (of 100 marks) in English for students of Class X. The marks obtained by students are shown in the following table :
Marks obtained0-1010-2020-3030-4040-5050-6060-7070-8080-9090-100
Number of students124151525151021
Find the modal marks.
items.answer: The greatest frequency is 25, so the modal class is 50−60, with l = 50, f₁ = 25, f₀ = 15, f₂ = 15 and h = 10. Mode = 50 + [(25 − 15)/(2×25 − 15 − 15)] × 10 = 50 + (10/20) × 10 = 50 + 5 = 55. Hence the modal marks are 55.
items.ocr: The book's last line reads '= 50 + 10 = 55'; (10/20) × 10 is 5, and 50 + 5 = 55, so the printed answer 55 stands.

items.stem:
The following frequency distribution shows the number of runs scored by some batsman of India in one-day cricket matches :
Run scored2000-40004000-60006000-80008000-1000010000-12000
Number of batsmen981021
Find the mode for the above data.
items.answer: The greatest frequency is 10, so the modal class is 6000−8000, with l = 6000, f₀ = 8, f₁ = 10, f₂ = 2 and h = 2000. Mode = 6000 + [(10 − 8)/(2×10 − 8 − 2)] × 2000 = 6000 + (2/10) × 2000 = 6000 + 400 = 6400. Hence the mode is 6400 runs.

items.stem:
A group of students conducted a survey of their locality to collect the data regarding number of plants and recorded it in the following table :
Number of plants0-33-66-99-1212-15
Number of houses24512
Find the mode for the above data.
items.answer: The greatest frequency is 5, so the modal class is 6−9, with l = 6, f₁ = 5, f₀ = 4, f₂ = 1 and h = 3. Mode = 6 + [(5 − 4)/(2×5 − 4 − 1)] × 3 = 6 + (1/5) × 3 = 6 + 0.6 = 6.6. Hence the mode is 6.6 plants.

items.stem:
If the median for the following frequency distribution is 28.5, find the value of x and y :
ClassFrequency
0-105
10-20x
20-3020
30-4015
40-50y
50-605
Total60
items.answer:
The cumulative frequencies are 5, x + 5, x + 25, x + 40, x + y + 40 and x + y + 45. Since N = 60, x + y + 45 = 60, so x + y = 15. … (1)
The median 28.5 lies in 20−30, so the median class is 20−30, with l = 20, F = x + 5, f = 20, N/2 = 30 and h = 10. Median = l + [(N/2 − F)/f] × h gives 28.5 = 20 + {[30 − (x + 5)]/20} × 10, so 8.5 = (25 − x)/2, i.e. 25 − x = 17 and x = 8. From (1), y = 15 − 8 = 7. Hence x = 8 and y = 7.
items.ocr: The book writes 'Thus model class is 20-30' where it means the median class.

items.stem:
Find the mean and mode of the following frequency distribution :
Classes0-1010-2020-3030-4040-5050-6060-70
Frequency381015743
items.answer:
With class marks 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55, 65 the products fᵢxᵢ are 15, 120, 250, 525, 315, 220 and 195, so Σfᵢxᵢ = 1640 and Σfᵢ = 50. Mean = 1640 ÷ 50 = 32.8.
The greatest frequency is 15, so the modal class is 30−40, with l = 30, f₁ = 15, f₀ = 10, f₂ = 7 and h = 10. Mode = 30 + [(15 − 10)/(2×15 − 10 − 7)] × 10 = 30 + (5/13) × 10 = 30 + 3.85 = 33.85.
Hence the mean is 32.8 and the mode is 33.85.
items.concept: Extending central tendency to grouped data
items.ocr: The book writes 'Class 30-40 has the maximum frequency 35'; 35 is the class mark of 30-40, and its frequency is 15, which is what the mode working uses.

items.stem:
Find the mean of the following distribution by step deviation method :
Class0-1010-2020-3030-4040-5050-60
Frequency513201575
items.answer: The class marks are 5, 15, 25, 35, 45 and 55. Take the assumed mean a = 35 and h = 10, so uᵢ = −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and fᵢuᵢ = −15, −26, −20, 0, 7 and 10, giving Σfᵢuᵢ = −44 with Σfᵢ = 65. Mean = a + (Σfᵢuᵢ/Σfᵢ) × h = 35 + (−44/65) × 10 = 35 − 6.77. Hence the mean is about 28.24.
items.ocr: The stem and table are printed on page 28 and the solution table runs on to page 29. The book rounds 440/65 to 6.76 and prints 28.24; the exact value is 28.23.
